title: Scout findings
description: What a model returns to a scout client. The model proposes; the client decides what is filed. Nothing here grants permission to create an issue -- the client applies the limits, checks for duplicates, and owns every GitHub write. Deliberately narrow so it survives the JSON Schema subsets that constrained decoding accepts.

findings.description: Candidate improvements, most valuable first. May be empty, and often should be: a repository with nothing bounded and evidence-backed to fix is a normal result, not a failure.

title.description: Issue title without a prefix. The client adds '[scout] '.

body.description: Issue body in Markdown: what is wrong, why it matters, and what a bounded change looks like. Omit the PR linkage section -- the client appends it so every implementation closes its source issue.

evidence.description: Where this was observed on the default branch: file paths, line ranges, quoted lines, or a doc section. A finding whose evidence cannot be pointed at is speculation and must not be returned.

confidence.description: How certain the finding is real and worth filing. Clients may drop anything below a configured floor.

area.description: Optional free-form area, such as a component or subsystem, for grouping in reports.

skipped.description: Findings deliberately not returned, and why. Distinguishes 'nothing to fix' from 'plenty to fix but not worth filing yet', which is the difference between a healthy repository and a full backlog.

title.description: What the skipped finding would have been called.

reason.description: Why it was not returned: already covered by an open issue or pull request, needs a human decision, too large for one focused change, or no default-branch evidence.

notes.description: Optional free text for the run report. Never used to decide what is filed.
